question: Which of the following correctly describes the SI unit of electric power and the commercial unit of electrical energy, respectively?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Watt (W); Kilowatt-hour (kWh)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Electric Power** is defined as the rate at which electrical energy is consumed or dissipated in an electrical circuit. It represents how fast work is being done by an electric current.
 
• The **SI unit** of electric power is the **Watt (W)**. One **Watt** is equivalent to **1 Joule per second (1 J/s)**. This means if an appliance uses one joule of energy every second, its power rating is one watt.
 
• **Electrical Energy** refers to the total energy consumed by an electrical appliance over a specific duration. It is calculated by the product of power and time (**Energy = Power × Time**).
 
• The **commercial unit** of electrical energy is the **Kilowatt-hour (kWh)**. This unit is used for billing purposes in households and industries because the standard SI unit (Joule) is too small to represent large-scale energy consumption conveniently.
